identity.mechanic: **Laid to rest:** a friendly unit is laid to rest when it dies or is sold, in a fight or while recruiting, by any cause and from any tribe. Death and sale are one event, so sell triggers fire in fights and death triggers fire in the shop. A turn is one Recruit Phase and the fight after it, so "Twice a turn" and "last turn" include that fight.

keywords.name: Fruit
keywords.text: When this is laid to rest, summon a Sprout in its slot.

identity.plays: The Guild doesn't fear losing units. It plans the order of its funerals. Fruit units in the front row turn every enemy kill into a slot that refills bigger. Fruit units in the back die last, when the count is highest. In the shop, selling stops being a loss: a sold Fruit unit leaves a Sprout in its slot, and sell triggers make the shop, the board and the gold grow. "Any tribe" in *laid to rest* is the Johnny door. An Ooze eating in the shop, a Bird flying South, a Bog tank dying under its Mire: all of them feed the Guild, and Guild cards that hand out Fruit turn other tribes' units into mourners.

units.name: Stumpwick Apprentice
units.golden: Fruit. Its Sprout has double stats.

units.name: Hired Mute
units.text: When a friendly unit is laid to rest, this permanently gains +1 Attack. Twice a turn.

units.name: Moss-Bier Bearer
units.text: Fruit. When played: give another friendly unit Fruit permanently.
units.golden: Fruit. When played: give two other friendly units Fruit permanently.

units.name: Funeral Steward
units.text: Once a turn, when a friendly unit is laid to rest while recruiting, gain 1 gold.

units.name: Black-Gloved Undertaker
units.text: Start of Combat: destroy the friendly unit beside this on its left. This gains its Attack.
units.golden: Start of Combat: destroy the friendly unit beside this on its left. This gains double its Attack.

units.name: Stinkhorn, Herald
units.text: Your non-Sprout units beside this have Fruit.
units.golden: Your non-Sprout units next to this have Fruit.

units.name: Clerk Inkcap
units.text: When a friendly unit is laid to rest, give a random other friendly unit +1/+1 permanently, and this loses 1 Health permanently. Three times a turn. (In a fight, both count now and after the fight. This can destroy it.)
units.golden: When a friendly unit is laid to rest, give a random other friendly unit +2/+2 permanently, and this loses 2 Health permanently. Three times a turn. (In a fight, both count now and after the fight. This can destroy it.)

units.name: Foxfire Lamplighter
units.text: Start of Combat: gain +1/+1 for every 4 units in the Register.
units.golden: Start of Combat: gain +2/+2 for every 4 units in the Register.

units.name: Ludwig, the Lodger
units.text: Can't be sold. Start of Turn: permanently gain +1/+1 for each friendly unit laid to rest last turn (at most +6/+6).

units.name: Bootlace Cordwainer
units.text: Your Fruit triggers twice. (The second Sprout goes to the nearest empty slot.)

units.name: Litter Pallbearer
units.text: Fruit. Your Sprouts also gain half the stats of the unit they came from.
units.golden: Fruit. Your Sprouts also gain the full stats of the unit they came from.

units.name: Sexton of the Litter Acre
units.text: Units in your shop have +1/+1 for each friendly unit laid to rest while recruiting this turn (at most +6/+6).

units.name: Bellows Puffwell
units.text: When a friendly unit is laid to rest while recruiting, permanently give your other Guild units +1/+1. Three times a turn.

units.name: Raindrop Puffball
units.text: Fruit. When this dies, give your other units +1/+1 for every two friendly units laid to rest this fight.

units.name: Warden Amanita
units.text: An enemy that kills a friendly unit takes damage equal to twice the number of friendly units laid to rest this fight.

units.name: Grandmother Bootlace
units.text: Your Sprouts have +1/+1 for every 3 units in the Register.

units.name: Candlesnuff Abbess
units.text: In fights, your Sprouts have Fruit. Six times a fight.

units.name: Old Fingers, Gravedigger
units.text: Start of Combat: summon copies of the last 2 non-Sprout units laid to rest this game into empty slots, with the stats they had then. The copies have Fruit.
units.golden: Start of Combat: summon copies of the last 4 non-Sprout units laid to rest this game into empty slots, with the stats they had then. The copies have Fruit.

extras.name: Sprout
extras.text: a Guild unit, X/X, with no text. X is the number of friendly units laid to rest **this fight**, or **this turn while recruiting**, counting the one it came from, at the moment it is summoned. Its size is then fixed; buffs add to it. Sprouts summoned while recruiting stay, keeping that size. Sprouts summoned in a fight last that fight. A Sprout counts as having started the fight if the unit it came from did.

extras.name: The Register
extras.text: (tribe counter, like the Larder or the Toll): the number of friendly units laid to rest this game, Sprouts included. It never goes down. The hero frame shows it.

builds.name: The Procession (fight).
builds.text: Fruit units across the front (Apprentice, Bier Bearer, Pallbearer, and anything beside Stinkhorn), with Crape Spinner and Cordwainer behind. Each enemy kill makes a larger slot, often two. Capstones: Candlesnuff Abbess, which chains Sprouts six times a fight, and Grandmother Bootlace, which scales every Sprout with the game's dead. Raindrop Puffball is the late burst. A Sprout from a unit that started the fight counts for hero damage, so a won Procession hits hard.

builds.name: The Wake (shop).
builds.text: Sell on purpose every turn. Mute, Steward and Sexton from the early tiers; Bellows Puffwell as the direction card; Ludwig grows off the count; Inkcap spends it; Foxfire Lamplighter fights with the Register. The loop is buy a Fruit unit, sell it, sell its Sprout. That's two laid-to-rest events for 2 net gold (three with Cordwainer): a buffed shop, two or three Bellows triggers and next turn's Ludwig growth. Old Fingers keeps the best sold units fighting.

builds.name: The Undertaker's Bargain (mixed).
builds.text: The Guild as a host for other tribes' death effects. Bier Bearer and Stinkhorn give Fruit to non-Guild units, Undertaker opens an Ooze's Belly at Start of Combat, and Amanita punishes every kill the enemy makes. Played with 3–4 Guild units and a second tribe's core.

builds.name: Oozes
builds.text: Eat in the shop is a death, so it is laid to rest. An Ooze eating a Fruit unit gains the stats and leaves a Sprout. Undertaker opens Bellies early.

builds.name: Birds
builds.text: Fly South is a sale, so it is laid to rest and triggers Bellows, Sexton and Steward. Old Fingers fights a copy of the Bird while it's away. Watch for the Nest Egg filling the slot Old Fingers needs.

builds.name: Bog folk
builds.text: Mire tanks in front die on purpose, and Fruit refills the slot. Note the refill is not Mired.

builds.name: Fairies
builds.text: a Ring under a Fruit slot buffs every Sprout that grows there.

builds.name: Hedgerow
builds.text: Sprouts can become the "rightmost unit" that Pass feeds, and Pass and Supper keep Inkcap alive.

builds.name: Hunters
builds.text: the weakest pairing. Pack beside Sprouts works, but Hunters want survivors.

risks: **Sell loops.** Laid to rest folds sales into deaths, which opens shop loops. I closed the obvious ones: Candlesnuff works in fights only, Stinkhorn's Fruit skips Sprouts, Sprouts still sell for 0, and Bellows, Sexton, Ludwig and Inkcap have caps. Even so, Cordwainer + Pallbearer + Bellows + Sexton is the combo to simulate first.
**Hero damage.** A Sprout counts as having started the fight only if the unit it came from did. Sprouts from Old Fingers' copies don't, so that board still hits softer than it wins.
**Board as HP.** Undertaker's self-kill early in a fight gives a Sprout with X=1, which is a real cost. He could be a trap card for new players.
**Rules needed:** is Eat a "death" (I assume yes)? Is Fly South a "sale" (I assume yes)? Does a copy summoned at Start of Combat get its own Start of Combat (I assume no)?

**Old Fingers can whiff** on a full board. That is intended tension, but it needs clear UI ("no empty slot"). Show the last two non-Sprout units laid to rest beside the Register, so a player sees what he will dig up.
**Readability.** In a long fight, a slot can refill many times with growing numbers. Animation has to show the Sprout grow out of the dead unit, or the chain reads as noise.
**Spike tracking load:** three counts (this fight, this turn, the Register). The hero frame should show them.
**Hunters lobby** gives the Guild little to feed on outside its own units.
**Ludwig can't be sold.** The drawback is deliberate, but it blocks sell triggers on him and makes it awkward to clear his slot.

tier_check.note: Apprentice (tempo, 4 stats plus a Sprout) and Mute (seed, +2 permanent a turn, target ~1.6). On guide.
Crape Spinner (buffer, ~6 in fight with 2–3 Sprouts), Bier Bearer (enabler, a lasting Fruit), Steward (economy, ~1 gold a turn, a third of a unit). On guide.

Stinkhorn and Undertaker (enablers), Inkcap (buffer, ~6 a turn against ~5.6, then dies by design), Lamplighter (combat engine, +5/+5 at a Register of 20, +10/+10 at 40, against 5–10 in fight). Lamplighter runs high late on purpose, as the mid-tier Register reader. Inkcap's 1/8 body is above the body target on purpose, because its Health is fuel.

Pallbearer and Ludwig (buffers; Ludwig ~10–12 a turn against ~11), Cordwainer (multiplier), Sexton (economy, ~8–12 stats of shop buffs bought a turn). On guide. Cordwainer is the first multiplier, as the guide expects.

Bellows (direction, ~36 permanent a turn at the cap against ~24 target and ~60 top), Raindrop (combat engine, ~48 in fight against ~48), Amanita (tempo, ~30 retaliation damage plus a 12 body). Bellows is high on purpose because it is the sell build's whole reason.

Bootlace and Candlesnuff (capstones, ~70–90 in fight each against ~84), Old Fingers (payoff: two copies of buffed units, around 40 stats plus their text and a Sprout each). Together with Cordwainer, the capstones go well past ×4. That is the golden-ceiling high roll, and it is bounded by "six times a fight" and by fights ending.

rationale: Wrote the three moments first. All three are "losing a unit refills something bigger", so that became the core.
Folded sale into death ("laid to rest"), so the shop moment and the fight moment run on the same triggers. This is the main Johnny lever.
Sprouts take the dead unit's slot, because the board is HP and gaps never close. The slot refills rather than the board shrinking.
Sprout size is the count laid to rest so far, so death order becomes a positioning puzzle (front dies early and small, back dies late and big).
"Any tribe" in laid to rest, so Ooze Eat, Bird Fly South and Bog tanks plug in without Guild-specific text.
Fruit is grantable (Bier Bearer, Stinkhorn), so other tribes' units can be the mourners.
Added the Register as one lasting count for the across-the-game moment. Only Bootlace reads it, to keep the counters few.
Capped every shop-side trigger (twice, three times, at most +6) after tracing the buy-sell-Sprout loop. Candlesnuff works in fights only for the same reason.
Kept Sprouts selling for 0. Paying for them made each Fruit unit gold-neutral to cycle.
Gave Inkcap a built-in death, so a buffer is also a fuse and Health buffs become fuel. This is the "outside its intended purpose" use.
Made Old Fingers need empty slots, so selling and digging up compete with Fruit refills. That is a choice, not a bonus.
Names and lore came last, matched to the brief's figures by job: Bootlace scales from below, Inkcap writes himself away, Bellows hosts the feast.

changes.what: Added one line: a turn is a Recruit Phase plus the fight after it.
changes.why: Settles "Twice a turn" and "last turn" on Mute, Inkcap and Ludwig for the whole tribe.

changes.what: Sprout size is fixed when summoned; shop Sprouts keep it. Sprouts inherit 'started the fight' from their source.
changes.why: Size was unreadable as a live count. Procession boards now deal hero damage when they win.

changes.what: Stinkhorn now gives Fruit only to non-Sprout units beside it.
changes.why: Closes the free sell loop: a Sprout beside him refilled itself forever in the shop.

changes.what: Health loss is plainly permanent; in a fight it counts now and after.
changes.why: "Permanently loses Health" inside a fight had no clear meaning.

changes.what: Wording: "the friendly unit beside this on its left".
Now Start of Combat: gain +1/+1 for every 4 units in the Register.
changes.why: It repeated Crape Spinner's Sprout buff; the Register needed a reader before Tier 6.
Ties the gravedigger into the Procession: dug-up units refill their slots too.
